messages:
alex: quick question about keystore-svc for private deploys — we need strict isolation for on-prem customers. goal: pod-level mTLS to our local KMS-proxy, and only allow egress from the keystore pods to the proxy/bastion IPs. what should netpol + RBAC + audit look like?

priya: +1 on per-pod egress. prefer NetworkPolicy with namespace+label selectors rather than IP whitelists where possible. for HSM/bastion we can allow by CIDR but keep it minimal. also we should enable `egress` deny-by-default on the namespace.

matt: sample netpol ive used:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-egress-lockdown
  namespace: private-keystore
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.4.2.0/28 # on-prem bastion/HSM
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
This gives us pod-to-proxy within cluster and allowed HSM CIDR.

priya: RBAC note — keystore pods should run under a dedicated ServiceAccount `sa-keystore`. only bind the minimum Roles: secrets get/list/watch for cert secrets, and a custom role for reading `kms-credentials` configmaps. do NOT give cluster-admin.

matt: role snippet:
```yaml
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: keystore-min-role
  namespace: private-keystore
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```
then RoleBinding to `sa-keystore`.

sec-bot: auto-check: run `pod-pss` and `netpol-lint` against the namespace. found 1 advisory: missing egress deny-by-default. recommended fix: add `ingress: []`/`egress: []` explicit deny policy.

alex: good catch. on audit logging — we need all KMS/encryption operations logged and forwarded to customer SIEM. thoughts on approach for private deployments?

priya: two parts: 1) app-level audit: keystore must emit structured logs for every KMS call (request id, caller SA, operation, result, latency). 2) platform-level: kube-audit + fluentd/rsyslog sidecar forwarding to customer collector over mTLS. ensure logs are signed/timestamped and retention config in the deployment manifest.

matt: we should mount a read-only secret with client certs for the forwarder and rotate monthly. example annotation for fluentd: `logging.company.com/forwarder: "mTLS:enabled;dest=https://logs.customer.local:6514"`

oncall-sam: incident response note — test the whole chain with a tabletop: simulate cert compromise for `sa-keystore` and run playbook to rotate keys, revoke certs, and isolate the namespace. we should add a kill-switch that patches netpol to deny all egress in <30s.

alex: how do we implement the kill-switch safely?

matt: pre-create a "deny-all" NetworkPolicy manifest and `kubectl apply -f deny-all.yaml` is the kill action. store the manifest in the ops repo and give oncall a runbook with the exact command. also add an automation that can apply it via the console with RBAC limited to SRE+oncall.

priya: also ensure audit trails capture who applied the deny-all. require `--record` or use the internal deploy system which attaches principal metadata.

sec-bot: vuln triage: there's a recent CVE on the fluentd plugin we use (CVE-2024-xxxx). action items: upgrade plugin to fixed release, run `image-scan` on all clusters, add runtime egress rule to prevent outbound to unapproved registries during rolling update.

alex: thanks all. action items I will take: 1) open PR with netpol + Role/RoleBinding + deny-all manifest, 2) draft runbook for kill-switch and rotation steps, 3) schedule tabletop with sec + oncall next week.

oncall-sam: will join the tabletop. also propose a 20m drill to verify we can apply deny-all and still recover.

matt: linking internal notes: https://intranet.redwood/ops/keystore-hardening (will add netpol/roles there).

alex: ok PR incoming, ping when tests pass. :thumbsup:
